claims.citation: The Sun (New York), 16 August 1866, p. 4, col. 4

claims.verbatim:
Ship Columbia, Robinson, Liverpool July 5, with mdse. and 53 pass
to Chas. H. Marshall & Co. Aug. 12, lat. 39 32, long. 69, fell in with
brig Nebraska of and from Boston for Galveston, with both masts
gone below the tops. Sent the mate and a boat's crew on board, but
she needed no assistance, but wished to be reported as making the[?] [cut]
Newport. [The above disaster has been previously reported.]

claims.claim: Brought news from Vera Cruz, to 1866-07-02
claims.citation: New York Herald, 12 July 1866, p. 8, col. 1
claims.verbatim:
We have also received via the
Solient[?] to Havana and the Columbia to this port corres-
pondence from Vera Cruz to July 2 and the city of
Mexico to June 29.

claims.citation: New York Herald, 17 August 1866, p. 2, col. 3
claims.verbatim:
The steamship Columbia, Captain Barton, from Ha-
vana on the 12th inst., arrived at this port yesterday.
We are under obligations to the purser for the prompt
delivery of our files and despatches.
